Noah (new-hire): hey team, first day question — my app connects to local psql fine but when I run `docker compose up` the app in the web container errors: `could not connect to server: No such file or directory "/var/run/postgresql/.s.PGSQL.5432"`. I've got PGHOST unset on the host.

Zoe (backend): welcome Noah :wave: that socket path error means the container is trying to use a unix domain socket. Inside a container the host's Unix socket isn't available. Are you using a host bind like `- /var/run/postgresql:/var/run/postgresql`?

Noah (new-hire): no bind. I think psql picks socket by default when PGHOST is empty. On my laptop `psql` connects via the socket and works, but the container has no socket so it fails.

Ravi (infra): exactly. Two options: 1) configure the app in container to use TCP by setting PGHOST=postgres (the service name), or 2) mount the host socket into the container (not recommended on mac). Prefer for dev to set PGHOST=postgres in compose env for the web service.

Zoe (backend): quick repro commands we recommend: `docker compose run --rm web env | grep PGHOST` to confirm. If empty, add override: `environment: PGHOST: postgres`. Or run `psql -h postgres` from inside web to test connectivity.

Noah (new-hire): set PGHOST=postgres in docker-compose.override.yml and `docker compose run --rm web bundle exec rails db:migrate` worked. Thanks y'all. I'll open a docs PR to mention socket vs TCP gotcha for new hires.

infra-bot: Welcome Noah! You were added to #new-hires. If you hit infra issues ping @Ravi. :robot_face:
